rationale: Preassign flower IDs and calibration/confirmatory roles so later threshold-basis rows cannot be reused as confirmatory evidence.

Focal P. rex barrier effectiveness under natural bumblebee pollination remains the highest-risk intervention component; this cohort supplies G effect/selectivity evidence but no longer defines the natural timing window.
Separate natural-state sentinel flowers estimate pollination-completion and attack/swelling chronology so timing gates are not inferred from investigator-selected barrier application times.
No focal P. rex >=5-level realized-exsertion manipulation with registered off-target checks has been recovered.
Same-flower repeatability is absent from published focal data; nesting repeated measurements in P0 CAL_A flowers avoids a separate field cohort while supporting 13 measurement-noise floors.

Focal supplementation effect is unresolved, but the treatment family has five congeneric supplementation precedents plus focal pollinator dependence and high outcrossing, so method risk is lower than G or graded P0.
